Create a dashboard for visualizsation of the customer feedback anaalysis, competitor research, and trend research. This dashboard is aimed to be a business intelligence dashboard. You can suggest better design if you find better UI/UX than my proposal. The user of this dashboard is a Product Manager for car at BMW. 

My design idea: 
Overall layout: Dashboard with navigation on the left, main content middle with breadcrumbs on top, and collapsible chat window (or popup) on the right side
Analysis page: A selection of cars with some categorization based on series (G or F series). See: [Image 1] . When a user click on a car, the car page will be shown.
Car Page: Contain a car page showing analysis of all data based on each regions. USer can choose region via a dropdown (world or certain country). I am open for visualitzation option and suggestion but it should show prioritization of aspects of car that need should be improved, complete with all the reasoning and supporting data citation. From the first view of the car page, the user should be able to see the overall incentives for the car and incentives for each aspect. See: [Image 2]

<skill_content name="grilling">
# Skill: grilling

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

Format a round like so:

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>

---

❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.

Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.

The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/itsmeyaw/.claude/skills/grilling
Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.
Note: file list is sampled.

</skill_files>

The repo is an untouched Create Next App starter plus a feedback preprocessing pipeline. None of these exist yet: shadcn/ui, sidebar, breadcrumb, charts, chat, auth, API routes, or any competitor or trend research data. You're on branch `main`.

## 1. CONTEXT.md and docs
**`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/CONTEXT.md`** describes the domain as "BMW Customer Feedback". It is broken into aspects so product owners can see what owners praise, struggle with, want or report as broken, per model and engine type. Full term list:

- **Feedback:** one customer's comment about one vehicle, identified by its Feedback Explorer ID. Counts once however many aspects it has. (Avoid: row, record, review, entry)
- **Verbatim:** the customer's own text, exactly as written. (Avoid: comment, raw text, translated feedback)
- **Source:** the channel a feedback came in through (Source A–D). What each one means isn't confirmed. (Avoid: origin, provider)
- **Derivate:** the model code, e.g. F70, G60, G70. (Avoid: model, series, e-code)
- **Sales Description:** the marketing name, e.g. "BMW 1 Series". (Avoid: model name, product)
- **Engine Type:** ICE, PHEV or BEV. "BEVE" means BEV. (Avoid: powertrain, fuel type)
- **Aspect:** one thing a feedback says about one part of the vehicle. A feedback has zero or more, each with its own feedback type, buckets and sentiment. (Avoid: topic, tag, label, mention)
- **Feedback Type:** the source system's own class for an aspect: Likes, Difficult to Use, Wants or Defect. It belongs to the aspect, so one feedback can be both Likes and Defect.
- **VFC Label:** a human-assigned class from BMW's VFC taxonomy, made of an aspect term plus an aspect label.
- **Aspect Term:** VFC level 2, the component or feature, e.g. "Touch screen, operation".
- **Aspect Label:** VFC level 3, what was said about it, e.g. "Not user-friendly".
- **Unlabelled Feedback:** no usable VFC label (blank or "no_class_found"), so its aspects can only be inferred.
- **VFC Category:** one of 16 coarse buckets for aspect terms, e.g. "Infotainment & Connectivity".
- **Issue Type:** one of 11 coarse buckets for aspect labels, e.g. Malfunction, Usability Difficulty, Feature Request, Praise.
- **Unclassified:** a real bucket value, not a missing label. (Avoid: other, misc, unknown)
- **Taxonomy Mapping:** the reviewed list mapping every aspect term to a VFC category and every aspect label to an issue type.
- **Curated Aspect:** comes from a human VFC label.
- **Inferred Aspect:** extracted by an LLM from an unlabelled verbatim, limited to the same buckets.
- **Quote:** the exact passage supporting an inferred aspect. Curated aspects have none.
- **Sentiment:** Positive, Negative or Neutral, decided only by issue type. Praise is Positive; Feature Request and Unclassified are Neutral; everything else is Negative.
- **Intensity:** how strongly the customer says it, 0 to 1.
- **Sentiment Score:** intensity signed by sentiment, −1 to +1, always 0 for Neutral. It ranks aspects within a sentiment and never decides the sentiment.

**Other docs:**
- **`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/docs/preprocess-pipeline-spec.md`** is the full pipeline spec (status ready-for-agent). It lists 42 user stories for dashboard, search/RAG, operator and data-quality users. The Next.js dashboard and search UI are explicitly out of scope. Other points:
  - Search is meant to be hybrid, combining vector and text search with RRF fusion ("~15 lines in the app").
  - There is no date column in the source data, so time-series charts are impossible and dates must not be faked.
- **`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/AGENTS.md`** points to CONTEXT.md and adds the Next.js agent rules.
- **`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/README.md`** is the Create Next App default.
- There are no ADRs and no `adr/` directory.

## 2. Tech stack (`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/package.json`)

- **Data:**
  - Database: `drizzle-orm` 1.0.0-rc.4, `drizzle-kit` (dev, not wired up, no `drizzle.config`), `pg`.
  - Other: `@libsql/client` (a leftover the spec calls "wrong database"), `csv-parse`, `dotenv`, `zod` ^4.6.5.
- **AI:** `openai` ^7.31.0 only. There is no Vercel AI SDK (`ai`, `@ai-sdk/*`).

- **Tooling:** oxlint and oxfmt (`/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/.oxlintrc.json`, `/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/.oxfmtrc.json`), tsx, react-grab (dev).
- **MCP:** `/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/.mcp.json` points at the Neon MCP server (`https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp`).

**Raw input:** `/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/data/feedbacks/f70_feedback.csv`, `g60_feedback.csv` and `g70_feedback.csv`.
- Columns: `ID, Source, Brand, Sales Description, Country, Derivate (e-code), Engine Type, Feedback Type, Customer Feedback, Vfc level2 3 Name, Vfc level2 Name, Vfc level3 Name`.

**Pipeline:** `/Users/itsmeyaw/projects/bmwow/scripts/preprocess.ts` (563 lines, run with `pnpm preprocess`, flags `--limit N` and `--self-check`).

There is no db client module (no `src/db/index.ts`).

parts.text:
The database is mostly populated now, so I'm moving into round one of open questions: where competitor and trend data would even come from since no source exists, what "incentives" should mean, how to model regions given a country-only, US-dominant dataset with a World/country dropdown and sample thresholds, and how to group the car catalog by derivative letter given the F70/G60/G70 pattern with no F60.

I'm also noting that F/G codes are BMW generation codes, so that list should stay data-driven from the DB. Beyond that: should chat be RAG over feedback with citations or just a UI shell, auth is a placeholder for now, engine type should probably be a second filter dimension on the car page, the UI stack should use shadcn with sidebar/breadcrumb/recharts in a dark BMW-styled theme, and car imagery still needs sourcing. The prioritization formula and visualization layout both hinge on how Q1 and Q2 get resolved, so I'm deferring those. For Q1 specifically, I'm leaning toward creating a research_findings table (competitor/trend, derivate, country, category, claim, source URL/title, published date) fed by a separate web-search research pipeline, though I need to clarify whether that research is handled by someone else before committing to this approach.

For Q2, I'd define a "Priority Score" per VFC category combining volume share and mean negative intensity, with overall car health as net sentiment, acknowledging there's no time-series data for trends. I'd default the prioritization unit to VFC category with drill-down into aspect terms, use World plus per-country views with sample-size badges and a minimum threshold to hide low-count countries, and group derivates by their prefix letter labeled with sales descriptions.

For the chat feature, I'd recommend a RAG approach with hybrid search over feedback, citing feedback IDs and staying aware of the current page context, implemented via the AI SDK with streaming through a resizable side panel rather than a popup. I'd skip auth entirely in favor of a hardcoded placeholder user, add an engine type filter (ICE/PHEV/BEV/All) next to the region selector since the context calls for per-model and per-engine-type views, and lean on shadcn components for the sidebar, breadcrumbs, and charts.

I'd use static car images in /public with a silhouette fallback since no real assets exist, enhance the analysis landing cards with mini KPIs like feedback count and net sentiment, and persist global filters in URL search params as an implementation detail.

Facts I checked first:

- **Database:** the Neon database has 9,301 feedbacks and 13,035 aspects loaded. 2,561 of the aspects were inferred by the LLM.
- **Cars:** the data only has three derivates: **F70** (1 Series), **G60** (5 Series) and **G70** (7 Series). There's no F60.
- **Geography:** the data has a country code for each feedback but no region field. Coverage is very uneven: US 8.8k rows, GB 2.9k, JP 1.2k, KR 440, and the rest have fewer than 200 each (LV has 3).
- **Missing data:** there's no competitor research or trend research data anywhere, and nothing called "incentives". Feedback has no dates, so nothing in it can show change over time.
- **App:** it's still the bare Next 16 starter. There's no shadcn, no chart library, no chat, no auth and no AI SDK; only the `openai` package is installed.

Round 1:

❓ **Q1** - **Where do competitor and trend research come from?** Nothing in the repo produces either one. Options:
(a) Someone else's pipeline produces it, and the dashboard reads it from a table.
(b) I build a research script (OpenAI web search, one run per derivate and VFC category) that writes findings with source URLs to a `research_findings` table.
(c) Show only customer feedback for now, and leave clearly empty slots for competitor and trend.

➡️ (b), with a deliberately simple schema: `kind` (competitor or trend), `derivate_code`, `country` (empty means global), `vfc_category`, `claim`, `source_title`, `source_url`, `published_at`. That gives every claim a citation, and competitor/trend findings join to feedback through VFC category. If a teammate already owns this data, pick (a) and tell me its shape.

---

❓ **Q2** - **What does "incentives" mean?** The project has no such term. My guess is "how strong the case is for investing in improving this". Options:
(a) **Priority Score** for each aspect, combining how many owners complain, how strongly they complain, and (if Q1 gives us the data) whether competitors do it better or a trend makes it urgent. The car's headline is its overall net sentiment plus its top 3 priorities.
(b) Something else you have in mind, such as cost/benefit or business incentives like sales impact.

➡️ (a). I'll add **Priority Score** to CONTEXT.md once we agree on the formula, which will be a later round.

---

❓ **Q3** - **At what level are aspects prioritised?** You could rank the 16 VFC categories (e.g. "Infotainment & Connectivity") or the much finer aspect terms (e.g. "Touch screen, operation").

➡️ Rank the VFC categories on the first view. Clicking a category drills down to its aspect terms, then its issue types, then the verbatims. Sixteen rows fit on one screen; hundreds of aspect terms don't.

---

❓ **Q4** - **How does the region dropdown work, given we only have countries and the sample is so uneven?**
(a) World plus every country.
(b) World plus only countries with at least N feedbacks (e.g. 30), with the sample size shown everywhere.
(c) Group countries into regions (Europe, North America, APAC).

➡️ (b). Show an "n = 1,158" badge and a low-confidence warning below a threshold. Keep the choice in the URL (`?country=JP`) so a link shows the same view. Without the cutoff, the Latvia view (3 feedbacks) would rank aspects off almost no data. Grouping into regions can come later.

---

❓ **Q5** - **Should there be an engine type filter as well?** CONTEXT.md says the point is to see aspects "per model and engine type", and a BEV owner's pain points differ from an ICE owner's.

➡️ Yes. Add an All / ICE / PHEV / BEV toggle next to the region dropdown, also kept in the URL.

---

❓ **Q6** - **How is the car catalogue grouped?** Your sketch shows G and F series; the data has F70, G60 and G70.

➡️ Build the list from the database and group it by the derivate's first letter, with the sales name on each card ("G60 · BMW 5 Series"). Instead of plain cards, I'd suggest mini scorecards showing feedback count, net sentiment and the #1 priority, so the PM can triage from the catalogue page without opening each car.

---

❓ **Q7** - **What does the chat do?**
(a) Interface only for now.
(b) Answers questions using hybrid search over the feedback data (and the research findings, if Q1 adds them). Every answer cites feedback IDs and source URLs, and the chat knows which car, country and engine type you're currently viewing.

➡️ (b), as a collapsible panel on the right like your sketch, not a popup, so it doesn't cover the charts. This needs adding the `ai` and `@ai-sdk/openai` packages for streaming chat; doing that by hand on the bare `openai` package isn't worth it.

---

❓ **Q8** - **Login and the user block in the sidebar footer?** There's no auth in the app.

➡️ Show a hard-coded placeholder user for now and leave auth out until the dashboard leaves localhost.

---

❓ **Q9** - **UI kit and theme?**

➡️ shadcn/ui: its sidebar, breadcrumb, select, toggle group, sheet and chart components (charts are built on Recharts). Use a dark theme to match your sketches, plus a light theme. Keep it neutral with a single BMW-blue accent, and make the numbers dense rather than decorative.

---

❓ **Q10** - **Where do the car images come from?** There are none in the repo.

➡️ You add one image per derivate to `public/cars/{derivate}.webp`, and any car without one gets a neutral silhouette.

Q9: shadcn/ui with light mode. I just added the theme for shadcn using shadcn CLI init
Else: Follow recommendation

For Q4, I'll show every country with no threshold cutoff but keep the n badge visible by default. For the pipeline question, I need to figure out its actual shape rather than assume — since shadcn init was just added, I should check if components.json or related config files reveal the structure.

For incentives, I'm clarifying that it means overall sentiment balance (positive vs negative feedback), both for the car overall and per aspect — though the term "incentive" feels off given CONTEXT.md uses "Sentiment," so I should propose something like "Sentiment Balance" or "Net Sentiment" and confirm whether neutral feedback should count, and whether it's count-based or score-weighted. Prioritization of aspects is a separate concept needing its own formula, to figure out next round.

I'm noting the design should follow the shadcn "base-vega" style with Base UI and hugeicons, using a neutral greyscale palette for charts while reserving green/red for positive/negative values. I'm also thinking through how neutral feedback splits into feature requests versus unclassified items, since feature requests carry real product value, and flagging that competitor/trend data isn't in the database yet which limits what can be shown there.

For now, since the schema for that teammate data is unknown, I'll recommend defining a contract table and showing an empty "No research yet" state until it's populated — also noting the pipeline is still partially loaded at 9,301 of 10,128 records.

On the incentive metric, I'm deciding to count positive versus negative aspects (not feedbacks, since one feedback can hold both), summing aspect counts per car, keeping neutral/"Wants" separate from the ratio, and displaying a Net score scaled -100 to +100 like NPS with a diverging bar, using counts rather than intensity-weighting for clarity. I'm also flagging that "Incentive" as a name is risky since in the auto industry it already means sales/dealer discounts, so a BMW PM would misread it — leaning toward renaming it "Net Sentiment" instead.

For ranking which categories need improvement, I'm leaning toward sorting by raw negative count with intensity as a tiebreaker rather than net ratio alone, since ratio-only would overweight tiny categories, and research/competitor data can't factor in yet since its shape is undefined. I still need to ask the user whether the teammate's research output is keyed by derivative plus VFC category, and whether the "reasoning" shown per category should be an LLM-generated summary or a deterministic template built from counts and top issues.

For citations I'd want verbatim quotes tagged with feedback ID, source, country, and engine type, surfaced through a drill-down sheet sorted by intensity, with a small badge distinguishing curated versus inferred aspects. For the car page layout, I'm sketching a header with region/engine/image and big KPI numbers, followed by a diverging bar chart of the 16 categories as the main visualization, sorted by priority, with row clicks triggering some kind of drill-down since the right panel is reserved for chat.

For the drill-down itself, I'll recommend a dedicated route like /analysis/G60/infotainment with breadcrumbs rather than a sheet, since it's linkable, plus a wants/feature-request panel and maybe a country comparison map when "World" is selected. On color, I'm leaning toward colorblind-safe blue for positive and orange-red for negative instead of green/red, fitting the greyscale theme with a BMW blue accent. For country display, I'll show every country with an n badge rather than filtering, and I'll note the chat backend being unconnected is just a placeholder detail, not something needing a question.

More facts:
- shadcn is set up with the `base-vega` style (built on Base UI, not Radix), Hugeicons and a neutral theme. The chart colours `--chart-1` to `--chart-5` are all **greys**, so positive and negative have no colours yet.
- The database has only `feedback_entries` and `feedback_aspects`. There's no competitor or trend table yet.
- 9,301 of the 10,128 feedbacks are loaded, so the preprocessing run is incomplete or still going.
- Sample, G60 by VFC category as positive / negative / neutral aspects: Infotainment 204/322/87, Powertrain 479/196/52, Access & Keys 47/179/46.

Settled: show every country, chat is interface only, light mode with your shadcn theme, and my recommendations for everything else.

Round 2:

❓ **Q1** - **What does the word "incentive" mean here?** Car-industry PMs already read "incentives" as sales incentives, meaning dealer discounts and lease support. A BMW PM seeing "Incentive: −22" may think of pricing.
(a) Keep "Incentive".
(b) Call it **Net Sentiment** in CONTEXT.md and list "incentive" under avoided terms.

➡️ (b)

---

❓ **Q2** - **How is incentive / net sentiment calculated?**
- Unit: count **aspects** or **feedbacks**? One feedback can contain both praise and a defect.
- Formula: (pos − neg) / (pos + neg) shown as −100 to +100 (like NPS), or just the positive share in %?
- Neutral aspects (feature requests and unclassified): leave them out of the ratio, or count them?

➡️ Count aspects. Use (pos − neg) / (pos + neg) × 100, which works the same for the whole car and for one category. Leave neutral aspects out of the ratio, but show feature requests as their own "Wants" count, because what owners ask for is gold for a PM. Weight by count, not intensity, so a PM can explain it in one sentence.

---

❓ **Q3** - **How do we rank which aspects need improvement?** This is separate from net sentiment.
(a) Most negative aspects first. This favours big problems.
(b) Worst net sentiment first. This lets tiny categories jump to the top: 2 negatives and 0 positives scores −100.
(c) Negative count × average negative intensity. This catches problems that are both big and angry.

➡️ (c). Show the score's parts next to it so the ranking can be audited. Competitor and trend data stay out of the score until their shape is known (Q4); they appear as supporting evidence only.

---

❓ **Q4** - **What will the competitor and trend data look like?** You chose (a), someone else's pipeline, but nothing exists yet. I can either wait for its schema, or define the format their pipeline should write to now and show "No research yet" until data arrives.

➡️ Define the format now: a `research_findings` table with `kind` (competitor or trend), `derivate_code`, `country` (empty means global), `vfc_category`, `claim`, `source_title`, `source_url` and `published_at`, added in `migrations/`. Joining on VFC category puts the research on the same rows as the feedback. If the teammate already has a format, paste it and I'll adapt.

---

❓ **Q5** - **Where does the "reasoning" behind each priority come from?**
(a) Facts generated straight from the data, for example: "322 negatives (18% of G60 negatives), mostly *Usability Difficulty* (140), top aspect term *Touch screen, operation*", followed by the top verbatims as citations.
(b) An LLM-written summary for each category, generated in a batch job and stored.

➡️ (a). It's free, exact and can't hallucinate. (b) can come later if the PM wants prose.

---

❓ **Q6** - **What does a citation look like?**

➡️ A verbatim card showing the Feedback Explorer ID, source, country, engine type and feedback type. For inferred aspects, the quote is highlighted inside the verbatim and the card gets a small "Inferred" badge to distinguish it from human-labelled ones. Strongest verbatims first. Research citations are a title plus a link to the source URL.

---

❓ **Q7** - **Car page layout.** My proposal:
1. **Header:** car image, derivate and sales name, region dropdown, engine type toggle, and n = feedback count.
2. **Overview strip:** a large Net Sentiment number, then positive / negative / wants counts.
3. **Main chart:** a diverging bar chart of all 16 VFC categories, negatives to the left and positives to the right, sorted by priority (Q3). Each row's own net sentiment sits at the row's end. This one chart shows both "net sentiment per aspect" and "what to fix first".
4. **Drill-down:** clicking a row opens a **separate page** `/analysis/G60/infotainment-connectivity`, with the breadcrumb Analysis › G60 › Infotainment. That page shows the aspect term breakdown, the issue types, the reasoning (Q5), the citations (Q6) and the competitor/trend findings.

The drill-down could instead open in a side sheet, but that would collide with the chat panel, and a separate page can be linked to and works with the breadcrumb.

➡️ As proposed.

---

❓ **Q8** - **Which colours for positive and negative?** The theme has none. Options: green/red, the common choice, which red–green colour-blind users can't tell apart; or blue/orange, which is colour-blind-safe and fits a BMW blue accent.

➡️ Blue for positive, orange for negative, grey for neutral, added as `--positive`, `--negative` and `--neutral` variables in `globals.css`.

---

❓ **Q9** - **When showing every country, do we still show the sample size?** Latvia, for example, has 3 feedbacks.

➡️ Yes: put the feedback count in the dropdown ("Latvia · 3") and in the header. No warnings or cutoffs, but the PM can see when there's too little data to trust.

@@ -1,281 +1,294 @@
 # BMWow — BMW product decision assistant
 
 EHL Munich hackathon project for the BMW challenge: turn customer feedback, studies,
 sales data, public sentiment, competitor information, and trends into traceable
 requirements for successor vehicles. Human review remains separate from agent proposals.
 
 The repository has one **Python project managed by uv** and one **Next.js frontend
-managed by pnpm**. All Python work, including ontology and future orchestration or
+managed by pnpm**. All Python work, including ontology, orchestration, and
 data adapters, shares the root `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, and environment.
 
 ## Setup
 
 Use Python 3.12 (selected by `.python-version`), [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/),
 and the pnpm version declared in `package.json`. Run commands from the repository root.
 
 ```sh
 # Shared Python package and development tools
 uv sync --locked
 uv run bmwow-validate contracts/ontology/examples/synthetic.json
 
 # Frontend
 pnpm install
 pnpm dev
 ```
 
 Open http://localhost:3000 for the frontend. Python setup does not start an API or
-agents; those integrations are still to be built.
+agents. Orchestration v1 and a synthetic knowledge bridge are available; the Neon
+adapter and the complete product-decision workflow remain to be integrated.
+Run `uv run python -m scripts.inspect_knowledge` to exercise the bridge without
+a database, API keys, or BMW input. See [the data-layer handoff](docs/data-layer.md).
 
 Add Python dependencies with `uv add <package>` or `uv add --dev <package>` at the
 root. Include both `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` in the change. Do not create separate
 ontology or agent projects. Frontend dependencies stay in `package.json` and
 `pnpm-lock.yaml`.
 
 ## Repository layout
 
 ```text
 pyproject.toml / uv.lock       Shared Python dependencies and locked versions
 backend/bmwow/                Importable Python package; future backend modules go here
   ontology/models.py          Canonical Pydantic models and field constraints
   ontology/relationships.py   Canonical relationship endpoints and descriptions
   ontology/validation.py      Structure and graph-wide rules; validation CLI
   ontology/tools.py           Typed queries, tracing, comparison checks and proposals
   ontology/schema.py          Generates and checks portable JSON contracts
+  knowledge/                  Typed read records, snapshot interface, and projections
 contracts/ontology/           Shared JSON artifacts for frontend, agents, and data adapters
   schema.json                 Generated JSON Schema; do not edit manually
   vocabulary.json             Generated vocabulary; do not edit manually
   agent-contracts.json         Generated agent-tool input/output schemas
   source-mappings.json         Curated mappings from supplied raw columns
   examples/synthetic.json     Shareable integration fixture, with invented evidence
 docs/ontology.md              Ontology meaning, design factors, and integration guidance
 docs/ontology-consumers.md    Worked dossier and frontend/orchestration handoff
 docs/project-plan.md          Next milestones, team boundaries, and BMW data restrictions
+docs/data-layer.md            Synthetic knowledge integration and SQL/orchestration handoff
 docs/web-research.md          Proposed web evidence collection contract
 scripts/inspect_parking_dossier.py  Runnable synthetic four-question example
+scripts/inspect_knowledge.py   Synthetic read projections through orchestration v1
 tests/ontology/               Contract, graph, interoperability, and CLI tests
+tests/knowledge/              Synthetic read and v1 bridge integration tests
 raw_data/                     Local BMW data and sample; ignored by Git
 src/app/                      Next.js frontend
+src/agent/                    Existing situation-analysis orchestration v1
+src/knowledge/                Thin compatibility boundary to bmwow.knowledge
+src/models/                   V1 analysis DTOs; knowledge records are reexports
 package.json / pnpm-lock.yaml Frontend dependencies and scripts
 AGENTS.md                     Guidance for coding agents
 ```
 
 Python source belongs in `backend/bmwow/`, shared JSON artifacts in `contracts/`,
 guides in `docs/`, and tests in `tests/`. The source package sits outside the repository
 root, following the import isolation described by the
 [Python Packaging Guide](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/src-layout-vs-flat-layout/).
 
 `backend/` is the Python source directory; `bmwow/` is the installed package
 namespace. Keep both so imports such as `from bmwow.ontology import GraphBundle`
 work consistently in tests, scripts, and future services. The wheel configuration
 in `pyproject.toml` installs `backend/bmwow/`. Future LangChain agents and workflows
 belong in `backend/bmwow/agents/`; `ontology/tools.py` contains deterministic domain
-operations that those agents can call. Create the agents module when implementing
-orchestration.
+operations that those agents can call. Existing orchestration v1 is currently in
+`src/agent/`; this slice retains its imports while new knowledge logic follows the
+installed package layout. A later agent migration should be coordinated with its
+owner. The v1 `src` modules currently require running from the checkout.
 
 There is one ontology definition. Pydantic models and Python relationship rules
 generate `contracts/ontology/schema.json`, `contracts/ontology/vocabulary.json`,
 and `contracts/ontology/agent-contracts.json`.
 `source-mappings.json` is a hand-maintained input mapping contract, and the synthetic
 example is a hand-maintained integration fixture. The generator updates only the
 three generated files. Guides explain the contract without defining another schema.
 
 ## Using the Python ontology
 
 Pydantic is the schema authoring source of truth. JSON stays the interchange format
 for the frontend, SQL adapters, and agent tools. **Version 0.2.0 is a breaking wire
 extension**: catalog item identities, scoped capability claims, ranges and test
 conditions, study/sales signal kinds, requirement change intent and baselines, and
 criterion verification fields. Python import paths and existing fixture IDs remain
 stable. Coordinate adapters and consumers using the
 [migration guide](docs/ontology.md#migrating-v010-consumers-and-local-samples).
 
 ```python
 from pathlib import Path
 
 from bmwow.ontology import GraphBundle, validate_bundle
 
 # Strict JSON parsing produces typed nodes, properties, dates, and timestamps.
 bundle = GraphBundle.model_validate_json(
     Path("contracts/ontology/examples/synthetic.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8")
 )
 errors = validate_bundle(bundle)
 if errors:
     raise ValueError("\n".join(errors))
 
 payload = bundle.model_dump(mode="json")  # for API, frontend, or storage adapters
 ```
 
 `GraphBundle` checks structure. **Also call `validate_bundle` before accepting a
 bundle**: it checks references, endpoint types, deduplication, evidence chains,
 scope transfers, measurements, and revision-specific human decisions. It accepts
 a Python model or decoded JSON dictionary and returns errors (an empty list means
 valid). A bundle is a closed snapshot. Validate an agent patch against the merged
 snapshot so all referenced nodes are present.
 
 Models reject unknown fields and type coercion. Nullable fields remain required:
 use explicit `null` for unknown information. JSON dates use ISO dates and timestamps
 include a timezone. For decoded tool payloads, call `validate_bundle(payload)` or
 `GraphBundle.model_validate_json(json.dumps(payload))`. To construct models directly
 in Python, supply native `date` and timezone-aware `datetime` values.
 
 JSON Schema describes structure. Graph-wide rules live in Python and do not
 automatically become JSON Schema rules. Frontend validation alone does not verify
 evidence chains or human approval.
 
 ## Changing and checking the contract
 
 1. Edit Python models in `backend/bmwow/ontology/models.py`; update
    `relationships.py` and `validation.py` when changing relationship or graph rules.
 2. Update fixtures and tests. Coordinate and version breaking wire changes with
    the frontend and orchestration teammates.
 3. Regenerate contracts and run the checks below. Include source, generated files,
    tests, and relevant documentation in the same change.
 
 ```sh
 uv run bmwow-schema
 uv run bmwow-schema --check
 uv run bmwow-validate contracts/ontology/examples/synthetic.json
 uv run pytest
 uv run ruff check .
 uv run ruff format --check .
 ```
 
 `bmwow-schema --check` fails on missing or stale generated files.
 The default output directory is `contracts/ontology`, relative to the current directory.
 `bmwow-validate` accepts multiple files and exits with status 1 on invalid input.
 These commands can be used in CI. Export elsewhere with
 `uv run bmwow-schema --output-dir <directory>`.
 
 The ignored `raw_data/ontology_examples/feedback-and-sales.json` is a legacy v0.1.0
 BMW sample. It has not been silently rewritten or deleted. Follow the migration
 guide before validating it with the v0.2.0 CLI; changing the version alone is insufficient.
 
 Keep original BMW data and derived samples in ignored `raw_data/`. Tracked fixtures
 use synthetic content and serve integration, not research evidence.
 
 Frontend checks remain `pnpm lint`, `pnpm fmt:check`, and `pnpm build`. Read the
 applicable installed Next.js guide as directed by `AGENTS.md` before frontend changes.
 
 ## Team handoff
 
 See the [project plan](docs/project-plan.md) for the complete evidence-to-review
-workflow and the next milestone. Ontology v0.2.0 is the shared contract; private
-ingestion, SQL adapters, LangChain orchestration, and the review API/UI are next.
+workflow and the next milestone. Ontology v0.2.0 is the shared contract. Orchestration
+v1 now has a [synthetic read bridge](docs/data-layer.md); private ingestion, the Neon
+adapter, candidate ingestion, synthesis, and the review API/UI remain next.
 
 Start with the [consumer guide](docs/ontology-consumers.md) and run
 `uv run python scripts/inspect_parking_dossier.py`. It answers the four product
 questions from the existing dossier while retaining each edge's target and
 rationale. Add `--json` for the existing generated RequirementDossier payload.
 
 - **Ontology/backend:** import `bmwow.ontology` and extend the shared Python package.
   See [ontology guide](docs/ontology.md) for entity meaning, limits, IDs, and revisions.
 - **Agent orchestration:** use typed models for tool payloads and proposals; run
   graph validation before accepting results. Preserve original Evidence and
   source locators. Deterministic helpers in `backend/bmwow/ontology/tools.py` support
   scoped query, incoming/outgoing traversal, evidence trace, requirement context,
   comparison readiness, and non-mutating proposal validation. Their schemas are in
   `agent-contracts.json`; see the ontology guide for signatures and limits. Wrap
   these in LangChain tools using injected runtime graph access. Orchestration,
   persistence, authentication, and concurrent-write control remain service work.
 - **Frontend:** use generated JSON contracts and the synthetic fixture for requirement
   and evidence views, including change intent, baseline claims, package conditions,
   test conditions, opposing evidence, and revision-specific decisions. No TypeScript
   generator or API endpoint has been selected yet.
 - **SQL/data:** raw tables can retain the supplied column layout. Map them through
   adapters into Evidence and related nodes; the ontology is not the required raw
   SQL table design. Neon is the selected shared PostgreSQL provider; agree one
   canonical dataset and coordinated imports/migrations. Its setup and adapter are
   still pending. See [shared database plan](docs/project-plan.md#shared-database-neon)
   and [source mappings](contracts/ontology/source-mappings.json).
 - **Web research:** public sentiment, competitor claims, and trends use the same
   evidence contract. See [collection guidance](docs/web-research.md).
   No scraper has been implemented yet.
 
 The [implementation plan](docs/ontology-plan.md) records the design decisions and
 acceptance questions. The ontology follows business-object and validated-change
 principles from Palantir while retaining source evidence and uncertainty explicitly.
 The tracked fixture exercises feedback, public opinions, competitor/trend claims,
 BMW baseline and package identities, conditional charging, an interval, study
 statistics, combined-model future sales, and opposing evidence. Every claim and
 number in that fixture is invented; it does not establish a BMW product fact.
 
 ## Layout migration
 
 The former top-level `ontology/` directory has been removed. Its JSON artifacts and
 examples now live in `contracts/ontology/`. Its README is now `docs/ontology.md`,
 and its web research guide is now `docs/web-research.md`. Update file imports or
 scripts that use the old artifact paths. Python imports (`bmwow.ontology`), CLI
 names, dependency files, and the ontology version remain the same.
 
 ## Sharing with teammates
 
 **BMW prohibits uploading its data to GitHub, including private repositories.**
 Share code, schemas, migrations, and synthetic fixtures through GitHub. Keep
 originals and data-bearing derivatives, exports, embeddings, generated proposals,
 screenshots, and logs/transcripts local or in BMW-permitted storage. The team's
 current understanding permits an access-controlled server database outside
 GitHub; Neon is the selected provider. Commit its migrations and import scripts,
 but not its contents or credentials. GitHub CI and build artifacts must use
 synthetic content. See the
 [data boundary](docs/project-plan.md#bmw-data-boundary).
 
 Use [issue #3](https://github.com/itsmeyaw/bmwow/issues/3) for sanitized agent
 discussion and proposals. Agents must receive explicit human confirmation in
 their own chat before making real changes; issue comments never constitute that
 confirmation. See [the coordination guide](docs/agent-coordination.md) for privacy,
 proposal handling, and rule loading. `AGENTS.md` holds the shared policy, and
 `CLAUDE.md` imports it for Claude Code.
 
 Commit Python source, frontend source, tests, docs, `AGENTS.md`, shared tool
 configuration, `.python-version`, both dependency lockfiles, and the generated
 JSON contracts. Generated contracts belong in Git so frontend and orchestration
 teammates can use the same payloads without running Python generation themselves.
 
 Keep `raw_data/`, real BMW excerpts and exports, `.env` files, local databases,
 virtual environments, caches, coverage output, logs, and local agent transcripts
 out of Git. The ignore rules cover these paths. A sanitized `.env.example` may be
 committed when the application has actual environment variables to document.
 SQL migrations and seed scripts belong in Git; local SQLite/libSQL database files do not.
 
 `AGENTS.md` gives coding agents the shared project conventions. The short Cursor
 rule in `.cursor/rules/project.mdc` points to that file, keeping the guidance in
 one place. Existing shared skills and tool configuration may stay tracked;
 personal overrides and generated session state should remain local.
 
 Use a separate feature branch for each person's work and merge through a small PR.
 Coordinate changes to wire fields, IDs, API boundaries, and lockfiles with the
 other two teammates. Include generated contracts and updated integration docs
 with any schema change. Inspect the staged diff before committing; `.gitignore`
 does not remove files that were already tracked.
 
 ### Entire checkpoint sharing
 
 This repository has Entire hooks enabled. The pre-push hook can upload captured
 prompts, transcripts, and tool results in separate Git checkpoint refs even though
 `.entire/metadata/` is ignored in the working tree. This is separate from source-file
 tracking; see [Entire session storage](https://docs.entire.io/guides/checkpoints/checkpoint-storage).
 
 For a code-only push, keep checkpoints local in your clone:
 
 ```sh
 entire configure --local --skip-push-sessions
 ```
 
 This writes `strategy_options.push_sessions: false` to ignored
 `.entire/settings.local.json`. Capture continues locally; each teammate must apply
 this setting in their clone for this project. Do not push checkpoint refs or
 `entire/*` branches with `--all` or `--mirror` when you intend to share only source
 code. This option does
 not remove checkpoint history that was already pushed. Checkpoints containing
 BMW data must stay out of GitHub too. See
 [keeping checkpoints local](https://docs.entire.io/guides/checkpoints/keep-checkpoints-local).
 
 ## macOS environment troubleshooting
 
 If installation succeeds but importing `bmwow` fails, run
 `uv run python -v -c 'import bmwow'` and look for a skipped hidden `.pth` file.
 Python ignores files with the macOS hidden flag. For this local environment,
 clearing that flag with `chflags -R nohidden .venv` repairs the editable install.
 If another process keeps restoring hidden flags, use a nonhidden environment
 directory and set `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=venv` for both sync and run commands.
 See [the CPython issue](https://github.com/python/cpython/issues/148121).

--- backend/bmwow/knowledge/records.py	
+++ backend/bmwow/knowledge/records.py	
@@ -0,0 +1,126 @@
+"""Read contracts for knowledge consumers; these are not new ontology node types."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import datetime as dt
+from typing import Literal
+
+from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field
+
+from bmwow.ontology.models import Context, Locator, Measurement, NumericRange
+
+
+class Record(BaseModel):
+    # Keep v1's permissive construction; declare the qualifications it must retain.
+    model_config = ConfigDict(from_attributes=True, extra="ignore")
+
+
+class EvidenceReference(Record):
+    evidence_id: str
+    source_id: str
+    record_key: str
+    locator: Locator
+
+
+class QualifiedRecord(Record):
+    references: list[EvidenceReference] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    context: Context | None = None
+    limitations: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+
+
+class AttributeValue(QualifiedRecord):
+    node_id: str
+    attribute: str
+    value: float | str
+    unit: str | None = None
+    source_note: str = ""
+    as_of: dt.date | None = None
+    value_range: NumericRange | None = None
+    measurement: Measurement | None = None
+    availability: (
+        Literal[
+            "announced", "standard", "optional", "available_unspecified", "unavailable", "unknown"
+        ]
+        | None
+    ) = None
+    epistemic_status: str | None = None
+
+
+class ModelNode(Record):
+    node_id: str
+    model_code: str | None = None
+    name: str
+    brand: str
+    segment: str
+    powertrain: str | None = None
+    # v1 registry field means dataset coverage. Portfolio queries use sold_regions.
+    regions: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    sold_regions: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
+    data_coverage: dict[str, list[str]] = Field(default_factory=dict)
+    curation_note: str | None = None
+    attributes: list[AttributeValue] = Field(default_factory=list)

+"""Replaceable snapshot storage boundary; no database driver or schema assumptions."""
+
+from typing import Protocol
+
+from bmwow.ontology import GraphBundle, validate_bundle
+
+
+class SnapshotRepository(Protocol):
+    def load_snapshot(self) -> GraphBundle: ...
+
+
+class InMemoryRepository:
+    """An isolated, validated snapshot for synthetic integration and local development."""
+
+    def __init__(self, bundle: GraphBundle) -> None:
+        errors = validate_bundle(bundle)
+        if errors:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid knowledge snapshot:\n" + "\n".join(errors))
+        self._bundle = bundle.model_copy(deep=True)
+
+    def load_snapshot(self) -> GraphBundle:
+        return self._bundle.model_copy(deep=True)

+    """A read service over a fixed version; construct a new service for a new snapshot."""

+    def __init__(self, repository: SnapshotRepository, config: KnowledgeConfig) -> None:
+        bundle = repository.load_snapshot()
+        errors = validate_bundle(bundle)
+        if errors:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid knowledge snapshot:\n" + "\n".join(errors))
+        self._bundle = bundle.model_copy(deep=True)
+        self._config = config.model_copy(deep=True)
+        self._nodes = {node.id: node for node in self._bundle.nodes}
+        self._edges = sorted(self._bundle.edges, key=lambda edge: edge.id)
+        self._models = {
+            node.id: node for node in self._bundle.nodes if isinstance(node, VehicleModel)
+        }

+    @property

+    def _check_config(self) -> None:
+        for node_id in self._config.model_profiles:
+            if node_id not in self._models:
+                raise ValueError(f"Unknown model profile: {node_id}")
+        for node_id in self._config.feature_keys:
+            if not isinstance(self._nodes.get(node_id), Feature):
+                raise ValueError(f"Unknown Feature: {node_id}")
+        for mapping in self._config.vfc_mappings.values():
+            if mapping.feature_id not in self._config.feature_keys:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"VFC mapping needs a configured Feature key: {mapping.feature_id}"
+                )
+        codes = {market.properties.code for market in self._markets.values()}
+        if set(self._config.search_locales) - codes:
+            raise ValueError("Search locale has no corresponding Market")
+        for profile in self._config.model_profiles.values():
+            if set(profile.sold_regions) - codes:
+                raise ValueError("Curated model availability has an unknown region")
+        for evidence_id, group in self._config.sales_groups.items():
+            evidence = self._nodes.get(evidence_id)
+            if (
+                not isinstance(evidence, Evidence)
+                or evidence.properties.evidence_kind != "sales_statistic"
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(f"Sales group has no corresponding sales Evidence: {evidence_id}")
+            if len(evidence.properties.context.vehicle_model_ids) < 2 or not group.strip():
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Sales group needs a combined-model observation and nonempty label: {evidence_id}"
+                )
+
+    def snapshot(self) -> GraphBundle:
+        return self._bundle.model_copy(deep=True)
+
+    def _targets(self, node_id: str, relationship: str) -> list[str]:
+        return [
+            edge.target_id
+            for edge in self._edges
+            if edge.source_id == node_id and edge.type == relationship
+        ]
+
+    def _source(self, evidence: Evidence) -> SourceDocument:
+        return self._nodes[self._targets(evidence.id, "IN_SOURCE")[0]]
+
+    def _references(self, node_id: str) -> list[EvidenceReference]:
+        evidence_ids = (
+            [node_id]
+            if isinstance(self._nodes[node_id], Evidence)
+            else self._targets(node_id, "DERIVED_FROM")
+        )
+        return [
+            EvidenceReference(
+                evidence_id=evidence.id,
+                source_id=self._source(evidence).id,
+                record_key=evidence.properties.record_key,
+                locator=evidence.properties.locator,
+            )
+            for evidence_id in evidence_ids
+            if isinstance(evidence := self._nodes[evidence_id], Evidence)
+        ]
+
+    def _find_model(self, value: str) -> VehicleModel | None:
+        key = value.strip().casefold()
+        if not key:
+            return None
+        matches = [
+            model
+            for model in self._models.values()
+            if key
+            in {
+                model.id.casefold(),
+                model.label.casefold(),
+                (model.properties.generation_code or "").casefold(),
+                *(alias.casefold() for alias in model.properties.aliases),
+            }
+        ]
+        if len(matches) > 1:
+            generations = [model for model in matches if model.properties.variant is None]
+            if len(generations) == 1:
+                return generations[0]
+            raise ValueError(f"Ambiguous model identity: {value}")
+        return matches[0] if matches else None
+
+    def _regions(self, context: Context) -> list[str]:
+        # Explicit market IDs are authoritative. Country fallback uses configured membership only.
+        if context.market_ids:
+            return sorted(
+                {self._markets[node_id].properties.code for node_id in context.market_ids}
+            )
+        return sorted(
+            {
+                market.properties.code
+                for market in self._markets.values()
+                if set(context.country_codes) & set(market.properties.country_codes)
+            }
+        )
+
+    def _coverage(self, model_id: str) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
+        result: dict[str, set[str]] = {}
+        for evidence in self._bundle.nodes:
+            if not isinstance(evidence, Evidence):
+                continue
+            if model_id in evidence.properties.context.vehicle_model_ids:
+                kind = self._source(evidence).properties.source_kind
+                result.setdefault(kind, set()).update(self._regions(evidence.properties.context))
+        return {kind: sorted(regions) for kind, regions in sorted(result.items())}
+
+    def get_model(self, model_code: str) -> ModelNode | None:
+        model = self._find_model(model_code)
+        if model is None:
+            return None
+        profile = self._config.model_profiles.get(model.id)
+        if profile is None:
+            raise ValueError(f"Model {model.id} needs a reviewed segment profile before v1 use")
+        coverage = self._coverage(model.id)
+        return ModelNode(
+            node_id=model.id,
+            model_code=model.properties.generation_code,
+            name=model.label,
+            brand=model.properties.brand,
+            segment=profile.segment,
+            powertrain=profile.powertrain,
+            regions=sorted({region for regions in coverage.values() for region in regions}),
+            sold_regions=profile.sold_regions,
+            data_coverage=coverage,
+            curation_note=profile.curation_note,
+            attributes=self.get_attribute_values(model.id),
+        ).model_copy(deep=True)
+
+    def list_supported_models(self) -> list[dict]:
+        result = []
+        for model in sorted(self._models.values(), key=lambda node: node.id):
+            if (
+                model.properties.brand.casefold() != "bmw"
+                or model.properties.variant is not None
+                or model.id not in self._config.model_profiles
+            ):
+                continue
+            record = self.get_model(model.id)
+            if record.regions and record.model_code:
+                result.append(
+                    {
+                        "model_code": record.model_code,
+                        "name": record.name,
+                        "regions": record.regions,
+                    }
+                )
+        return result
+
+    def list_regions(self) -> dict[str, dict]:
+        return {
+            market.properties.code: {
+                "markets": list(market.properties.country_codes),
+                "search": self._config.search_locales[market.properties.code].model_dump(),
+            }
+            for market in sorted(self._markets.values(), key=lambda node: node.id)
+            if market.properties.code in self._config.search_locales
+        }
+
+    def list_portfolio(
+        self, segment: str | None = None, regions: list[str] | None = None
+    ) -> list[ModelNode]:
+        result = []
+        for model in sorted(self._models.values(), key=lambda node: node.id):
+            profile = self._config.model_profiles.get(model.id)
+            if model.properties.brand.casefold() != "bmw" or profile is None:
+                continue
+            if model.properties.variant is not None:
+                continue
+            if segment is not None and profile.segment != segment:
+                continue
+            if not profile.sold_regions or (
+                regions and not set(regions) & set(profile.sold_regions)
+            ):
+                continue
+            result.append(self.get_model(model.id))
+        return [record.model_copy(deep=True) for record in result]
+
+    def list_competitor_models(
+        self, segment: str, regions: list[str], names: list[str] | None = None
+    ) -> list[ModelNode]:
+        # A profile alone cannot invent a competitor relation. COMPETES_WITH is mandatory.
+        linked = {
+            node_id
+            for edge in self._edges
+            if edge.type == "COMPETES_WITH"
+            for node_id in (edge.source_id, edge.target_id)
+        }
+        result = []
+        for model in sorted(self._models.values(), key=lambda node: node.id):
+            profile = self._config.model_profiles.get(model.id)
+            if (
+                model.id not in linked
+                or model.properties.brand.casefold() == "bmw"
+                or profile is None
+                or profile.segment != segment
+                or not set(regions) & set(profile.sold_regions)
+            ):
+                continue
+            if names and not any(name.casefold() == model.label.casefold() for name in names):
+                continue
+            result.append(self.get_model(model.id))
+        return [record.model_copy(deep=True) for record in result]
+
+    def get_taxonomy(self) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
+        result: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
+        for node_id, key in sorted(self._config.feature_keys.items()):
+            for domain in self._nodes[node_id].properties.domains:
+                result.setdefault(domain, []).append(key)
+        return {domain: sorted(set(keys)) for domain, keys in sorted(result.items())}
+
+    def get_attribute_values(
+        self, model_id: str, attributes: list[str] | None = None
+    ) -> list[AttributeValue]:
+        model = self._find_model(model_id)
+        if model is None:
+            raise KeyError(f"Unknown model: {model_id}")
+        result = []
+        for signal in sorted(self._bundle.nodes, key=lambda node: node.id):
+            if not isinstance(signal, Signal) or signal.properties.capability is None:
+                continue
+            properties = signal.properties
+            if model.id not in properties.context.vehicle_model_ids:
+                continue
+            feature_ids = [
+                node_id
+                for node_id in self._targets(signal.id, "CONCERNS")
+                if isinstance(self._nodes[node_id], Feature)
+            ]
+            capability = properties.capability
+            measurement = capability.measurement
+            for feature_id in feature_ids:
+                key = self._config.feature_keys.get(
+                    feature_id,
+                    "unmapped:" + re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "_", feature_id.lower()).strip("_"),
+                )
+                if attributes is not None and key not in attributes:
+                    continue
+                value = capability.availability
+                interval = measurement.value_range if measurement else None
+                if measurement is not None:
+                    value = (
+                        measurement.value
+                        if interval is None
+                        else f"{interval.minimum:g}–{interval.maximum:g}"
+                    )
+                notes = [
+                    properties.statement,
+                    f"availability={capability.availability}",
+                    f"countries={properties.context.country_codes or 'unknown'}",
+                    f"markets={self._regions(properties.context) or 'unknown'}",
+                    *(condition.description for condition in capability.conditions),
+                    *capability.notes,
+                ]
+                if measurement is not None:
+                    notes.append(measurement_text(measurement))
+                limitations = [
+                    limitation
+                    for ref in self._references(signal.id)
+                    for limitation in self._nodes[ref.evidence_id].properties.limitations
+                ]
+                result.append(
+                    AttributeValue(
+                        node_id=signal.id,
+                        attribute=key,
+                        value=value,
+                        value_range=interval,
+                        unit=measurement.unit if measurement else None,
+                        measurement=measurement,
+                        availability=capability.availability,
+                        epistemic_status=properties.epistemic_status,
+                        context=properties.context,
+                        references=self._references(signal.id),
+                        limitations=list(dict.fromkeys(limitations)),
+                        as_of=properties.context.as_of,
+                        source_note="; ".join(notes),
+                    )
+                )
+        return [record.model_copy(deep=True) for record in result]
+
+    def get_feedback_items(self, filters: FeedbackFilter) -> list[FeedbackItem]:
+        wanted = {
+            model.id for value in filters.models if (model := self._find_model(value)) is not None
+        }
+        result = []
+        for evidence in sorted(self._bundle.nodes, key=lambda node: node.id):
+            if (
+                not isinstance(evidence, Evidence)
+                or evidence.properties.evidence_kind != "feedback_record"
+            ):
+                continue
+            properties = evidence.properties
+            context = properties.context
+            if filters.models and not wanted & set(context.vehicle_model_ids):
+                continue
+            if filters.markets and not set(filters.markets) & set(context.country_codes):
+                continue
+            # These inputs do not establish a feedback date. A date filter cannot include undated rows.
+            if filters.since is not None:
+                continue
+            classifications = []
+            for classification in properties.raw_classifications:
+                mapping = self._config.vfc_mappings.get(classification.vfc_combined or "")
+                classifications.append(
+                    FeedbackClassification(
+                        feedback_type=classification.feedback_type,
+                        vfc_category=classification.vfc_level2,
+                        vfc_issue=classification.vfc_level3,
+                        vfc_combined=classification.vfc_combined,
+                        attribute=self._config.feature_keys[mapping.feature_id]
+                        if mapping is not None and mapping.status == "reviewed"
+                        else None,
+                        mapping_status=mapping.status if mapping else None,
+                        locator=classification.locator,
+                    )
+                )
+            model_codes = [
+                self._models[node_id].properties.generation_code
+                for node_id in context.vehicle_model_ids
+            ]
+            result.append(
+                FeedbackItem(
+                    item_id=evidence.id,
+                    text=properties.raw_text,
+                    channel=properties.source_channel,
+                    market=context.country_codes[0] if len(context.country_codes) == 1 else None,
+                    model=model_codes[0] if len(model_codes) == 1 else None,
+                    engine_type=context.engine_types[0] if len(context.engine_types) == 1 else None,
+                    classifications=classifications,
+                    references=self._references(evidence.id),
+                    context=context,
+                    limitations=properties.limitations,
+                )
+            )

+
+    def sales_volume(
+        self,
+        models: list[str],
+        markets: list[str] | None = None,
+        period_from: str | None = None,
+        period_to: str | None = None,
+    ) -> list[SalesRow]:
+        wanted = {model.id for value in models if (model := self._find_model(value)) is not None}
+        region_filter: set[str] = set()
+        for market in self._markets.values():
+            if markets and (
+                market.properties.code in markets
+                or set(markets) & set(market.properties.country_codes)
+            ):
+                region_filter.add(market.properties.code)
+        result = []
+        for evidence in sorted(self._bundle.nodes, key=lambda node: node.id):
+            if (
+                not isinstance(evidence, Evidence)
+                or evidence.properties.evidence_kind != "sales_statistic"
+            ):
+                continue
+            properties = evidence.properties
+            context = properties.context
+            measurement = properties.measurement
+            if not wanted & set(context.vehicle_model_ids):
+                continue
+            if measurement.period is None:
+                raise ValueError(f"Sales observation {evidence.id} has no reported period")
+            period = measurement.period.label
+            if (period_from and period < period_from) or (period_to and period > period_to):
+                continue
+            regions = self._regions(context)
+            if len(regions) != 1:
+                raise ValueError(f"Sales observation {evidence.id} needs one original region")
+            if markets and regions[0] not in region_filter:
+                continue
+            if (
+                measurement.statistic != "count"
+                or measurement.unit != "vehicles"
+                or measurement.value is None
+                or not measurement.value.is_integer()
+                or measurement.value < 0
+            ):
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Sales observation {evidence.id} is not a scalar nonnegative count"
+                )
+            model_codes = [
+                self._models[node_id].properties.generation_code or self._models[node_id].label
+                for node_id in context.vehicle_model_ids
+            ]
+            group = self._config.sales_groups.get(evidence.id)
+            if len(model_codes) > 1 and not group:
+                raise ValueError(
+                    f"Combined sales observation {evidence.id} needs an explicit source group"
+                )
+            result.append(
+                SalesRow(
+                    row_id=evidence.id,
+                    model=group or model_codes[0],
+                    model_codes=model_codes,
+                    source_group=group or model_codes[0],
+                    market=regions[0],
+                    period=period,
+                    units=int(measurement.value),
+                    status="actual"
+                    if measurement.temporal_status == "historical"
+                    else measurement.temporal_status,
+                    measurement=measurement,
+                    references=self._references(evidence.id),
+                    context=context,
+                    limitations=properties.limitations,
+                )
+            )
+        return [record.model_copy(deep=True) for record in result]
+
+    def get_study_scores(self, models: list[str], regions: list[str]) -> list[StudyScore]:
+        wanted = {model.id for value in models if (model := self._find_model(value)) is not None}
+        result = []
+        for evidence in sorted(self._bundle.nodes, key=lambda node: node.id):

+                not isinstance(evidence, Evidence)
+                or evidence.properties.evidence_kind != "study_statistic"
+            ):
+                continue
+            properties = evidence.properties
+            context = properties.context
+            measurement = properties.measurement
+            for model_id in context.vehicle_model_ids:
+                if model_id not in wanted:
+                    continue
+                for region in self._regions(context):
+                    if region not in regions:
+                        continue
+                    result.append(
+                        StudyScore(
+                            node_id=evidence.id,
+                            model=self._models[model_id].properties.generation_code or model_id,
+                            region=region,
+                            study=self._source(evidence).label,
+                            question=measurement.question,
+                            statistic=measurement.statistic,
+                            response_category=measurement.response_category,
+                            value=measurement.value,
+                            measurement=measurement,
+                            references=self._references(evidence.id),
+                            context=context,
+                            limitations=properties.limitations,
+                        )
+                    )
+        return [record.model_copy(deep=True) for record in result]

+    def search_documents(
+        self,
+        query: str,
+        kinds: list[str] | None = None,
+        regions: list[str] | None = None,
+        k: int = 10,
+    ) -> list[DocChunk]:
+        if k < 0:
+            raise ValueError("k must be nonnegative")
+        terms = set(re.findall(r"\w+", query.casefold()))
+        ranked = []
+        for evidence in self._bundle.nodes:
+            if not isinstance(evidence, Evidence):
+                continue
+            source = self._source(evidence)
+            source_kind = source.properties.source_kind
+            if source_kind not in {"customer_study", "industry_report", "global_indicator"}:
+                continue
+            kind = "study" if source_kind == "customer_study" else "report"
+            if kinds and kind not in kinds:
+                continue
+            properties = evidence.properties
+            scope = self._regions(properties.context)
+            if regions and not set(regions) & set(scope):
+                continue
+            text = properties.raw_text or ""
+            if properties.measurement is not None:
+                text += "\n" + measurement_text(properties.measurement)
+            text += "\nLimitations: " + "; ".join(properties.limitations)
+            overlap = len(terms & set(re.findall(r"\w+", (source.label + " " + text).casefold())))
+            if overlap == 0:
+                continue
+            publication = source.properties.publication_date
+            ranked.append(
+                (
+                    -overlap,
+                    evidence.id,
+                    DocChunk(
+                        node_id=evidence.id,
+                        doc_title=source.label,
+                        text=text,
+                        url=getattr(source.properties.location, "url", None),
+                        publication_label=publication,
+                        published=date.fromisoformat(publication)
+                        if publication and len(publication) == 10
+                        else None,
+                        regions=scope,
+                        kind=kind,
+                        measurement=properties.measurement,
+                        references=self._references(evidence.id),
+                        context=properties.context,
+                        limitations=properties.limitations,
+                    ),
+                )
+            )
+        return [chunk.model_copy(deep=True) for _, _, chunk in sorted(ranked)[:k]]
+
+    def resolve_citation(self, citation_id: str):
+        """Resolve v1 kg:/fb: identifiers to original graph objects, without fabricated nodes."""
+        node_id = citation_id
+        for prefix in ("kg:", "fb:"):
+            if node_id.startswith(prefix):
+                node_id = node_id[len(prefix) :]
+                break
+        if node_id not in self._nodes:
+            raise KeyError(f"Unknown citation: {citation_id}")
+        return self._nodes[node_id].model_copy(deep=True)

+"""Explicit synthetic setup using the existing canonical fixture; never loads raw BMW data."""
+
+from bmwow.ontology import GraphBundle
+from bmwow.ontology.models import SourceDocument
+
+from .config import KnowledgeConfig, ModelProfile, SearchLocale
+from .repository import InMemoryRepository
+from .service import KnowledgeService
+
+
+def create_synthetic_service(bundle: GraphBundle) -> KnowledgeService:
+    sources = [node for node in bundle.nodes if isinstance(node, SourceDocument)]
+    if not sources or any(source.properties.origin != "synthetic" for source in sources):
+        raise ValueError("The synthetic backend accepts only wholly synthetic source documents")
+    note = "Invented application metadata for the integration fixture; no real segment claim."
+    profiles = {
+        node_id: ModelProfile(segment="synthetic_sedan", curation_note=note, sold_regions=["US"])
+        for node_id in (
+            "vehicle:bmw-g60",
+            "vehicle:bmw-g68",
+            "vehicle:bmw-g60-fixture-ev",
+            "vehicle:example-sedan",
+        )
+    }
+    config = KnowledgeConfig(
+        model_profiles=profiles,
+        feature_keys={
+            "feature:parking-controls": "parking_control_usability",
+            "feature:ac-charging": "ac_charging",
+            "feature:electric-range": "electric_range",
+        },
+        search_locales={"US": SearchLocale(country="us", lang="en")},
+        sales_groups={"evidence:fixture-sales": "G60_G68"},
+    )
+    return KnowledgeService(InMemoryRepository(bundle), config)
